question: What did Apple spend on R&D and SG&A, and how did that change relative to revenue?

answer.summary: In FY2023, Apple spent $29.91B on R&D, up 14.0% YoY from $26.25B in FY2022 [F00028][F00029], while SG&A spending was $24.93B, down 0.6% YoY from $25.09B in FY2022 [F00031][F00032]. Revenue fell 2.8% YoY to $383.29B in FY2023 from $394.33B in FY2022 [F00013][F00014]. R&D grew at more than five times the rate of the revenue decline, so R&D intensity rose relative to revenue, whereas SG&A declined slightly less than revenue, also raising SG&A intensity modestly. The revenue decline was driven primarily by Mac, which fell $10.82B (-26.9%), accounting for 98% of the total revenue change [F00282], and by the Americas segment, which fell $7.10B (-4.2%), accounting for 64% of the total change [F00838], partially offset by Services growth of $7.07B (+9.1%) [F00010]. Management attributes the revenue weakness to foreign currency headwinds and lower Mac and iPhone net sales [T00275].
drivers: Mac was the largest contributor to the revenue decline (-$10.82B, 98% of the total change) [F00282]
Americas was the largest contributor to the revenue decline by business segment (-$7.10B, 64% of the total change) [F00838]
Services growth of $7.07B (+9.1%) offset 64% of the revenue decline [F00010]
risks_and_red_flags: R&D spending grew 14.0% while revenue declined 2.8%, indicating rising R&D intensity relative to revenue [F00028][F00013]
Mac weakness drove the revenue decline, with Mac net sales falling $10.82B (-26.9%) [F00282]
Americas segment revenue fell $7.10B (-4.2%), the largest segment-level contributor to the revenue decline [F00838]
No forward-looking guidance on R&D or SG&A provided in the retrieved evidence

outlook.actuals_view: FY2023 R&D and SG&A both rose relative to revenue as revenue declined 2.8% YoY [F00013]
